subject: Tips for reparameterizing / scaling a nonlinear model?

messages.author: 2567ef0395c70306
messages.subject: Tips for reparameterizing / scaling a nonlinear model?
parts:
Hi all,

   I have a fairly simple model relating temperature (T) to a log-linear rate of pathogen die-off (K) across a number of experimental data. The model essentially consists of a normal likelihood relating each mean natural log concentration (C) at time (t), and with sample standard devation (s) and sample size (n) to a linear function of K. K, in turn, is related to T through a normal distribution around an exponential function. K is not log transformed because a few experiments have negative values (i.e. there is population growth). For observation i in experiment j:

C[i] ~ Normal ( C_0[j] - K[j] * t[i] , s[i] / sqrt(n[i]) )

K[j] ~ Normal ( K_25 * exp( lambda * (T[j] - 25) , sigma_K )

There are currently 18 experiments with a total of 170 observations in the model.

If I scale t, C, and s, use noncentral parameterizations for K and C_0, and omit the temperature function, such that K is simply estimated separately for each experiment with a common prior distribution, I can run 5000 iterations within about 45 minutes.

On the other hand, if I include the temperature dependency function, A). I'm not sure how best to handle data / parameter scaling of K and T, due to the exponential function used to relate them, along with the fact that sometimes K <= 0, and B). The model takes up to 20 hours to run the same number of iterations, despite the fact that less parameters are actually estimated.

My guess is that the exponential term is really bogging things down. Is there a better way to parameterize or scale this model that might improve its speed?

Would rescaling temperature, then maybe reparameterizing the exponential term as ln (K[j] - sigma_K * Z_k[j]) / K25 = lambda * T be likely to help?

Apologies if this question is very basic or I'm missing something obvious.
